  "concordance_definition": "The paper defines concordance by the ability of animal tests to predict human responses, specifically regarding efficacy and toxicity/safety. It emphasizes the use of Likelihood Ratios (LRs) as the appropriate metric for assessing this predictive power, as they incorporate sensitivity and specificity and are independent of prevalence.",
  "limitations_stated": [
    "Monticello et al. study used only 182 drugs compared to >3200 in the authors' work.",
    "Monticello et al. study looked only at animal test/Phase I concordance, not later phase clinical trials.",
    "Monticello et al. study used few, broad categories for adverse drug reactions.",
    "Monticello et al. study combined mice and rats as 'one effective species'.",
    "Clark and Steger-Hartmann study did not show or weigh predictive aspects against areas where they were lower, non-existent, or negative.",
    "Some examples provided by Clark and Steger-Hartmann were only just over the statistical threshold they had set.",
    "The absence of toxicity in animals provides essentially no insight into the likelihood of a similar lack of toxicity in humans.",
    "More than 90% of drugs that appeared safe and effective in animals failed in human trials between 2006 and 2015.",
    "Animal tests have never met, and could never meet, the standards of validation applied to alternative methods."
  ],
  "funding_conflict": "The corresponding author's employer, Cruelty Free International, is a not-for-profit organisation that campaigns for an end to animal experiments. However, the Trust did not play any role in the design, analysis or interpretation of the study, or in the writing of the manuscript. The authors declare no financial competing interests. Monticello et al. reported no conflicts of interest but thanked almost 20 biopharmaceutical companies and had affiliations to nine companies.",
  "key_numbers": [
    "If a new drug has a 70% chance of not being toxic in humans, a negative test in any of the five species (dogs, rats, mice, rabbits, monkeys) will increase this probability to an average of just 74%.",
    "Dogs and monkeys were the least predictive species, raising the probability from 70% to just 72% and 70.4% respectively.",
    "Monticello et al. reported a mean inverse Negative LR (iNLR) of just 1.5–1.6.",
    "Monticello et al. reported a mean Positive LR (PLR) of 2.9.",
    "Of Monticello et al.'s 36 possible results, only two PLRs/LR+ met the authors’ acknowledged ‘diagnostic’ definition of a value of >= 10, and none of the iNLRs/iLR- did so.",
    "30 of the iLR- values reported by Monticello et al. were <= 2, with most of these in or around unity.",
    "More than 90% of the drugs that appeared to be safe and effective in animals went on to fail in human trials between 2006 and 2015.",
    "Between 2008 and 2014, 29 FDA clinical hold orders were actioned, seven for unexpected deaths, and nine involving unexpected target organ damage."
  ]
